subject: Urgent: Hosted API queue saturation causing latency spikes

Subject: Escalation: queue saturation on Hosted API — immediate triage requested

Team —

Acme (and a subset of other hosted customers) report p95/p99 regressions and elevated error rates starting ~07:45 PDT. Key metrics:
- p95 increase: ~180ms -> ~1.2s
- p99 spikes: up to ~3.8s
- error rate on gen endpoints: ~5% (timeouts/502)
- sustained request backlog observed in queue metrics

Customer impact: checkout failures, partial loss of revenue for Acme. They want ETA and mitigation.

Please triage: Markus, can you pull queue depth, batching metrics, and recent config changes? If this is a serving config/regression, we need an emergency rollback path or immediate mitigation (reduce batch sizes, cap queue depth, spin up extra workers).

Cc'ing Rishi due to potential exec escalation/credits.

Thanks — Neha
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-18T09:05:00-07:00
Subject: RE: Escalation: queue saturation on Hosted API — initial findings + mitigation

Quick summary of findings from the serving plane: 
- Root signal: sustained increase in queue depth on the hosted GPU pools starting 07:40 PDT. Queue depth rose above the configured soft-cap (350) and reached bursts to ~820 on two pools.
- Probable trigger: an infra config change deployed on 2026-03-16 increased the default continuous-batching max_window and loosened the queue depth cap for 'efficiency mode' (commit 9f4c2). That change interacts poorly with the traffic distribution we saw this morning (more long sequences + spikey bursts), causing batch build times to increase and backlog to form.
- Observable effect: longer batch build times -> higher per-request latency -> queue growth -> more timeouts (feedback loop). p95/p99 regressions follow this pattern.

Immediate mitigations we executed (09:00–09:15):
1) Temporarily reduced continuous-batching max_window from 120ms -> 45ms for affected pools.
2) Enforced a hard queue-depth cap of 400 (was accidentally unbounded for some pools under the new flag).
3) Auto-scaled additional worker nodes in the affected region to add capacity (+20% workers) and enabled faster warmup.
4) Rolled an emergency config patch to revert the 'efficiency mode' cap loosening; full rollback scheduled if metrics don't recover.

Current status (09:05): p95 down from 1.2s -> ~300ms; p99 trending down. Error rate reduced to ~0.9%. We're continuing to monitor.

Next steps:
- Monitor for 2 hours and observe if queue depth stabilizes.
- Postmortem + RCA draft in ~24 hours.
- Evaluate if we need a permanent change to default batching heuristics and add a safety kill-switch to prevent unbounded queue growth.

Attached: investigation-notes.md, grafana_snapshot_20260318.png

— Markus
Director, Serving Infrastructure

Hi Jane —

Thank you for your patience. Full status update: our serving team implemented emergency mitigations this morning (reduced batch window, enforced queue cap, added workers, and rolled a config patch). Observed effects:
- p95 for your tenant: returned to ~200–320ms (back near baseline)
- p99: returned to expected band and continuing to improve
- Error rate: down to <1%

We will follow up with a formal RCA and a draft postmortem within 24 hours. Monica will reach out about a goodwill credit (we've proposed 10% for the impacted billing period) and to schedule a technical post-incident review with your engineering team.

Apologies for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority. If you'd like an immediate call with our serving engineers, we can spin up a bridge now.
